description: Fig. 6 is a single-panel X-ray diffraction (XRD) figure showing four vertically offset diffractograms, labelled from bottom to top 0Cr (black), 3Cr (blue), 6Cr (red) and 9Cr (green). The abscissa is 2θ (degree) spanning 30–100°; the ordinate is Intensity (a.u.) with no printed numeric scale. All four patterns display the same suite of labelled reflections: γ(111) near 42–43°, δ(110) near 44–45°, γ(200) near 49–50°, δ(200) near 65°, γ(220) near 72°, δ(211) near 82°, γ(311) near 88° and γ(222) near 95°, identifying austenite (γ) plus ferrite (δ). The distinguishing feature is a reflection labelled κ(111) at approximately 41.4°, visible only in the bottom 0Cr pattern as a small peak/shoulder immediately to the left of γ(111); it is absent in the 3Cr, 6Cr and 9Cr traces. Relative peak intensities of γ(111)/δ(110)/γ(200) differ somewhat between compositions but the phase set is the same. The figure demonstrates that annealing at 550 °C for 5 h leaves the austenite+ferrite assemblage unchanged, while κ-carbide precipitation occurs in the Cr-free strip and is suppressed by Cr addition.

observations.observation: Four XRD patterns are stacked with vertical offsets and colour-coded: 0Cr (black, bottom), 3Cr (blue), 6Cr (red) and 9Cr (green, top).
The abscissa is labelled 2θ (degree) with tick marks at 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100; the ordinate is labelled Intensity(a.u) with no numeric values printed.
Reflections labelled γ(111), δ(110), γ(200), δ(200), γ(220), δ(211), γ(311) and γ(222) appear in all four patterns, indicating the coexistence of austenite (γ) and ferrite (δ).
A reflection labelled κ(111) is printed only on the 0Cr pattern, positioned near 41.4°, just to the left of the γ(111) peak.
The caption states the patterns are of Fe–28Mn–9Al-1.2C-xCr strips after annealing at 550 °C for 5 h.
The citing text states the constituent phases of the annealed strips are still austenite and ferrite.
The citing text states the (111) diffraction peak of κ-carbides at 41.4° obviously appears in the annealed 0Cr strip, suggesting annealing at 550 °C for 5 h promotes κ-carbide precipitation.
The citing text states that this κ-carbide peak is still not observed in the Cr-containing annealed strips, so Cr addition also suppresses κ-carbide precipitation even after annealing.
The dominant peaks in every trace lie in the 40–50° 2θ range (γ(111)/δ(110)/γ(200)), while the reflections at higher angles are markedly weaker.
